assessment: This manuscript addresses the cellular and dendritic physiology of cholinergic interneurons in the striatum. The authors use a creative integration of electrophysiology and optical methods to investigate this distinctive cell type, which is critically important at the intersection of motivated behavior and disease. They uncover a mechanism through which two separate active conductances – the hyperpolarization-activated h-current (HCN) and the persistent sodium current (NaP) – act in concert to selectively boost synaptic input from the thalamus onto proximal dendrites of cholinergic interneurons.
